findings.evidence: `Construct.lean:86-94` exposes `iidMixtureLaw` and immediately supplies `iidMixtureLaw_def`; `CoinFlips.lean:62-68` does the same with `coinKernel_toMeasure`.
findings.fix: Remove both `@[expose]` annotations and retain `iidMixtureLaw_def`/`coinKernel_toMeasure` as the public unfolding interface, using `:= (rfl)` if needed across visibility boundaries.
findings.issue: `iidMixtureLaw` and `coinKernel` (`CoinFlips.lean:62`) are both `@[expose]` even though exported characterization lemmas already provide access, coupling downstream proofs to implementation bodies.

findings.evidence: All three declarations lack attributes; the established analogous API uses `@[simp] theorem blockLaw_def`, `prefixLaw_def`, and `pathLaw_def` in `Exchangeability/Basic.lean:92-129`, and `@[simp] theorem deFinettiMeasure_toMeasure` in `DeFinetti/Mixture.lean:87-93`.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` to these lemmas, unless a concrete loop is demonstrated; this also makes the protected definitions usable without unfolding.
findings.issue: The characteristic normal forms `iidMixtureLaw_def`, `coinKernel_toMeasure` (`CoinFlips.lean:66`), and the closed evaluation `coinKernel_apply_true` (`CoinFlips.lean:71`) are not tagged `@[simp]`, so routine normalization requires manual rewriting.

summary: The new definitions unnecessarily expose their bodies, and their characteristic normal-form lemmas lack the project’s standard simplifier annotations.
